The test suite updates Span construction for the new end_timestamp_precise field but adds no test that: (1) a segment exceeding 1000 spans is truncated by the Lua script (data loss is untested and unasserted); (2) ZUNIONSTORE score aggregation (SUM across merged sets) doesn't corrupt eviction order; (3) mixed old-format (set) and new-format (zset) keys during a rolling deploy are handled — the Lua script calls ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE on keys that may still be plain sets from before the deploy, which returns a WRONGTYPE error and fails the whole EVALSHA pipeline for that batch. A rolling deploy of this consumer will hit WRONGTYPE errors on any segment key created by the old code until its TTL (redis_ttl=3600s) expires. There is no migration/compatibility handling and no test for it.

findings.title: Behavior change on audit log endpoint gated by an undocumented query parameter — API contract break for admin users
findings.body: Clients (including Sentry's own frontend and any admin tooling) that append `optimized_pagination=true` — or, more realistically, once this flag is documented/adopted — will get different cursor semantics (OptimizedCursorPaginator emits integer-floor datetime keys via the broken get_item_key, different cursor value encoding than DateTimePaginator's millisecond timestamps). DateTimePaginator encodes cursor values as milliseconds-since-epoch floats; OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key returns math.floor(datetime) which crashes, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (a number) which build_queryset then interpolates into a `datetime >= %s` SQL comparison — comparing a datetime column to an integer. The two paginators are not cursor-compatible, so a client that switches the flag mid-pagination gets corrupt cursors. The endpoint's publish_status is EXPERIMENTAL, but the flag is undocumented and the branch is controlled by request.user.is_superuser, meaning Sentry staff hitting the endpoint with the flag get a different (broken) response shape with no warning.
